text:
sec-bot: Detector: high entropy payload wrapped with our KMS key detected in gs://partners/ingest/2026-03-23/obj.enc — wrapping_key=projects/redwood/locations/us/keyRings/ingest/cryptoKeys/partner-wrap :warning:

rachel: @marco @tev oncall plz triage. Scanner found probable AWS creds encoded inside the wrapped blob. Looks like server-side wrap (our key).

marco: investigating. Metadata shows ingest service performed the wrap at 02:58 UTC. That implies plaintext existed before wrap. Possible causes: partner CI uploaded payload raw, or a local agent leaked env vars.

tev: containment suggestions:
- rotate partner-facing SA keys and revoke current key IDs (marco)
- create new key version for partner-wrap and set as primary (marco)
- run rewrap pipeline to re-encrypt objects under new version (marco+tev)
- patch ingest pipeline to client-side envelope-encrypt before upload + redact logs (tev)
- forward KMS decrypt events to sec-logs with 90d retention and add alert for any decrypt by non-ingest principal (rachel)

marco: doing revocation now. command (sanitized):
```
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete 04efab12 --iam-account=svc-partner-ingest@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
Applied temporary IAM deny for partner pipeline writes to storage.

marco: creating new key version for partner-wrap. rewrap plan: container job reads objects, calls KMS decrypt with old key (we keep access), then encrypt with new primary. Will write results to gs://partners/ingest-rewrapped. Estimate 2h for priority prefix.

tev: I'll open a small PR to add AES-GCM envelope client-side encrypt to the agent and drop full payloads from logs. Also adding a lint check to fail if payloads contain aws_access_key pattern.

rachel: please also capture evidence: copy the flagged object to evidence bucket and preserve SHA256. Legal, can you create a hold and advise partner notification wording?

legal: evidence hold created (CASE-2026-042). Drafting partner notification and coordinating with PM. Recommend limited disclosure: inform partner of suspected plaintext in their upload and request CI artifact retention for 30d.

marco: ticketed rewrap job and started initial run for the most recent folder. Progress: 120/240 objects rewrapped, no failure so far. Will throttle to avoid API quota.

tev: PR posted: https://git.internal/ingest-agent/pull/78. Changes: client-side envelope AES-GCM, log redaction, and config flag enable-encryption. Tests added.

rachel: once rewrap completes we need to rotate downstream secrets that may depend on the archived values. Create a short runbook for app owners: rotate secrets, confirm no copies retained in logs or CI artifacts, ack in ticket.

marco: also adding audit rule: forward KMS Decrypt events for partner-wrap to sec-logs and trigger pager if decrypt principal != svc-partner-ingest.

tev: note: backup/restore integration needs to accept new cipher headers. I'll add compatibility in restore tool to accept both old and new envelope formats.

rachel: owners and ETA: marco (SA key revoke + key-version create + temp deny) — 15m; marco+tev (rewrap job) — kickoff now, 3h throttled; tev (agent PR) — PR in 10m, rollout after rewrap; rachel (audit forwarder + alert) — 30m; legal (hold + partner comms) — 1h.

marco: revoke applied, deny binding in place, rewrap 50% done. Posting updates to incidents channel after run completes.

tev: redaction change merged to staging, will hold rollouts until rewrap finished.

rachel: good progress. After this incident, add a platform policy: require client-side envelope encryption for any third-party ingestion flows within 30 days and add scanner rule that flags server-wrapped blobs when the uploader identity is not a known trusted agent.

legal: partner notified via secure channel; awaiting ack.

rachel: thanks team — keep updates here and add any blockers. :white_check_mark:
